newsitem.title: KENYA: Police arrest hundreds in swoop in Nairobi.
newsitem.headline: Police arrest hundreds in swoop in Nairobi.

text.p: Police arrested more than 700 suspected criminals in a weekend swoop in central Nairobi and crowded slums around the city, Kenyan officials said on Sunday.
The operation, launched on Friday night and continuing on Saturday, was aimed at cracking down on car-jackers, illegal aliens and petty criminals, police said.
They said police seized a quantity of suspected stolen property during search operations which covered bars, illegal drinking dens, lodging houses and residential areas.
Kenyan president Daniel arap Moi and other leaders have recently called for stronger measures to combat street crime, car-jacking and general lawlessness in the Kenyan capital and in other towns.
The Sunday Standard reported that forged passports, air tickets, bank statements and other documents could be freely bought from a flourishing forgery racket in Nairobi.
A Standard reporter described how he travelled from Nairobi to Dar es Salaam on an air ticket bought for half-price from the forgers, and using a stolen U.S. passport supplied by them.
He said American, South African, New Zealand, Zambian and Tanzanian passports were on sale for up to 50,000 shillings ($1,000) from an apartment in central Nairobi.
